rules.sentence: In patients with systemic lupus erythematosus, immunosuppressive agents help control disease activity and improve platelet counts.
For those with Helicobacter pylori–associated thrombocytopenia, eradication therapy not only addresses the infection but also promotes hematologic recovery.[35][36]
Prophylactic platelet transfusions for preoperative thrombocytopenia are not well-supported by evidence and may potentially result in refractory thrombocytopenia.
Alternatively, immunosuppressants, thrombopoietin receptor agonists, and monoclonal antibodies have demonstrated effectiveness in normalizing platelet counts in some patients.
Intraoperatively, desmopressin and antifibrinolytic agents may be used prophylactically, while recombinant factor VII can be used to treat severe hemorrhage.[37]
